result.summary: Validates the field count for `outscript` and `in` command-line arguments in `bitcoin-tx`, throwing an error if more than three colon-separated fields are provided. It also clarifies the help string for `in` and adds test cases to `bitcoin-util-test.json` verifying both options fail on malformed inputs.
result.problem: `bitcoin-tx` only checked for a minimum number of colon-separated fields (< 2) on `outscript` and `in`. For `outscript`, flags were only read if exactly three fields were present; trailing or duplicate colons caused script flags to be silently ignored, yielding transactions paying to bare scripts instead of P2SH or P2WSH wrappers without throwing an error.
evidence: PR description demonstrates that `bitcoin-tx -create outscript=0:OP_DROP:S: nversion=1` exits with code 0 and produces a bare OP_DROP output instead of the requested P2SH script hash wrapper.
result.changed_since_previous: The change now also validates separator counts and error messages for `in=TXID:VOUT[:SEQUENCE_NUMBER]`, updates its argument help string, and adds a corresponding test case.
result.card: This PR updates bitcoin-tx to reject outscript and in arguments that contain too many colon-separated fields. Previously, outscript only processed flags when given exactly three parts, meaning trailing colons from typos silently dropped flags and generated transactions with bare scripts instead of P2SH or P2WSH wrappers while exiting 0. An extra field in the in parameter was likewise silently ignored. Both options now throw an invalid format error when passed more than three components.

risk.why: A bug would only cause bitcoin-tx CLI input parsing to reject valid inputs or fail to error on invalid ones.
